signature_ttp.technique: Modify Program, reprogramming safety controller logic

provenance: US Treasury sanctions action of October 2018 naming a Russian government research institute (TsNIIKhM); Dragos activity group reporting; MITRE ATT&CK for ICS.
what_this_card_cannot_tell_you: That the TRITON intrusion succeeded. It did not. The safety system tripped the plant because the attacker's code was wrong, which is how anyone found out. The most famous safety-system attack on record is also a story about an attacker failing.

sector_targeting: Targeted by protocol, not by sector

signature_ttp.technique: Unauthorized Command Message via native industrial protocols

provenance: CISA advisory AA22-103A, April 2022, issued jointly with DOE, NSA and FBI; Dragos PIPEDREAM reporting.
what_this_card_cannot_tell_you: Who this is. The toolkit was found before it was used, which is unusual and good, but it means attribution rests on capability analysis rather than on observed operations against a victim. This is the only card in my set where the tooling is better documented than the operator, and putting a confident name on the card would misrepresent that.

signature_ttp.technique: Supply Chain Compromise, trojanised ICS vendor software downloads

provenance: CISA advisory AA20-296A, October 2020; US DOJ indictment of March 2022 naming FSB Center 16 officers; CISA alert TA18-074A on energy sector intrusions.
what_this_card_cannot_tell_you: What the access was for. Public reporting describes years of persistent presence in energy sector networks with no destructive effect, which reads either as patient pre-positioning or as intelligence collection that never had an effect phase. The card has to pick a capability tier and the honest answer is that intent is unresolved.

aka: the Colonial Pipeline ransomware affiliate operation
sector_targeting: Selected by ability to pay, not by sector

signature_ttp.technique: Data Encrypted for Impact against IT systems, with OT consequences arising indirectly
signature_ttp.mitre_ics_id: T1486 (Enterprise; no ICS equivalent, because the technique never touched OT)

provenance: CISA and FBI joint advisory AA21-131A, May 2021; Colonial Pipeline public statements and subsequent congressional testimony.
what_this_card_cannot_tell_you: The most important thing here: the OT was never touched. The pipeline stopped because the operator could not bill with IT encrypted. A criminal group with no ICS capability caused a fuel disruption through a business-process dependency.

sector_targeting: Any facility running internet-exposed Unitronics PLCs

signature_ttp.technique: Internet Accessible Device, default credentials on exposed controllers

provenance: CISA advisory of December 2023 on IRGC-affiliated actors exploiting Unitronics PLCs, issued with FBI, NSA, EPA and INCD.
what_this_card_cannot_tell_you: Which tier this actor really belongs in. It brands itself hacktivist and the bar was low: exposed PLCs with default passwords. But CISA attributes the campaign to IRGC-affiliated actors. A capability tier is one field and this actor needs a paragraph.
